editorial_note: Five selected objects from a dated native tools/list catalog, not API responses or proof these five operations executed. Tool descriptions are provider claims. H10 outputs are full schemas; WH/Brandsearch outputs are not declared in these selected catalog objects. Public schema example identifiers are conservatively redacted. Object values otherwise preserved; enclosing index is editorial.

original.name: analyze_keywords
original.title: Keyword Batch Analysis
original.description: Helium 10 Keyword Research (formerly Cerebro). Batch enrichment for an explicit list of 1–200 keywords: one row per keyword with search volume, CPC, ABA top-3 click/conversion share, and H10 metrics (CPR, IQ score, title density, competing products). Use when the user already has a candidate-keyword set to score, rank, structure into ad groups, or cross-compare. Not for: deriving new terms from one seed (use get_keywords_by_keyword); reverse search on an ASIN (use get_keywords_by_asin). Note: output order does NOT match input order — match results by the phrase field.

keywords.title: Keywords

marketplace.description: Marketplace code: US, UK, DE, JP, etc.
marketplace.title: Marketplace

aba_conv_share.description: ABA Total Conv. Share — Gain valuable insights into the top 3 clicked products for each keyword;

keyword_sales_weekly.description: Keyword Sales — Estimated number of weekly sales (in number of units) attributed to each keyword

iq_score.description: Cerebro IQ Score — Score based on ratio of estimated search volume vs. number of competing products: a high score means a relatively high number of searches compared to the number of competitors; a low score means the opposite.

search_volume.description: Search Volume — Estimated number of times this keyword is searched monthly on Amazon.

title_density.description: Title Density — Number of page 1 products with the searched keyword in their title.

amazon_choice.description: Amazon Choice — Badge / label context for the phrase (see Amazon Choice filter semantics in the Cerebro UI).

original.name: get_product_profit_and_loss_summary
original.title: Product P&L Summary
original.description: Helium 10 Product P&L Summary (formerly Profits). Returns product-level P&L SNAPSHOTS — one row per product_level (sku | asin | parent_asin) with identity fields and a single Level 1 metrics map covering the WHOLE date range; NO time buckets, no trend, no breakdown trees. Use to rank products by profitability for one period, compare margin across the catalog, flag loss-making SKUs, build a product-level report. IMPORTANT: if the question mentions a TREND or change OVER TIME (daily/weekly, 'over the last N days', 'units sold trend', etc.) use get_product_profit_and_loss_summary_series instead — it ranks top-N AND returns the time series in one call. Not for: store-wide totals (use get_account_profit_and_loss_summary); per-product trends (use get_product_profit_and_loss_summary_series); per-product drill-down (use get_product_profit_and_loss_breakdown). A cost_of_goods or indirect_cost of 0 on any row may mean the cost was never configured rather than genuinely zero — data.caveats flags that when it happens. Verify with list_amazon_cogs / list_amazon_indirect_cost_settings before describing the figures as normal: net_profit and margin are upper bounds until you do.Comparing two periods? Both must span the same number of days: read data.meta.period_days from each response and require them to match. A 30-day window against a 31-day one inflates every percentage delta by roughly 2pp. If they differ, align the windows, switch to daily averages, or state the difference and its effect on every percentage you report.Amounts are converted into the requested currency per marketplace before aggregation; omitting marketplace means the figures are the combined total across every authorised marketplace, so say so when reporting them. data.meta echoes both.

current_date_from.description: Inclusive start calendar date in date_tz, YYYY-MM-DD only (no time). Use the exact parameter name current_date_from; do not use start_date, date_from, or from_date. Must be <= current_date_to.
current_date_from.title: Current Date From

current_date_to.description: Inclusive end calendar date in date_tz, YYYY-MM-DD only (no time). Use the exact parameter name current_date_to; do not use end_date, date_to, or to_date. Must be >= current_date_from. A value after today in date_tz is silently clamped to today in date_tz (the future has no data).
current_date_to.title: Current Date To

date_tz.description: Timezone used to interpret calendar dates. Must be one of the Amazon marketplace report timezones (not any IANA timezone). Examples: America/Los_Angeles, Europe/Paris, Europe/London. Italy/Germany/Spain use Europe/Paris (not Europe/Rome or Europe/Berlin). Do not pass a city name, abbreviation, or UTC offset. Optional; when omitted, defaults to the queried marketplace's report timezone (America/Los_Angeles when no single marketplace is set).
date_tz.title: Date Tz

product_level.description: Row aggregation: sku | asin | parent_asin. Parent ASIN groups child ASINs; one ASIN may map to multiple SKUs.
product_level.title: Product Level

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for amounts. Optional, defaults to USD.
currency.title: Currency

seller_ids.description: Optional. SQL IN filter on seller account IDs (array of strings). Profits intersects with sellers from Pacvue token; no intersection → empty result. Default null (all authorised sellers).
seller_ids.title: Seller Ids

marketplace.description: Optional marketplace filter as an array of region short codes ONLY (e.g. ['US', 'CA', 'MX']); Amazon SP-API marketplace IDs (e.g. '[REDACTED:PUBLIC_EXAMPLE_IDENTIFIER]'), seller IDs, and domains are rejected. Allowed: AE, AU, BE, BR, CA, CN, DE, EG, ES, FR, IE, IN, IT, JP, MX, NL, PL, SA, SE, SG, TR, UK, US, ZA. Default null (all authorised marketplaces).
marketplace.title: Marketplace

asins.description: Optional. SQL IN filter by ASIN list (array of strings, e.g. ['[REDACTED:PUBLIC_EXAMPLE_IDENTIFIER]']). Default null (all ASINs).
asins.title: Asins

skus.description: Optional. SQL IN filter by seller SKU list (array of strings). Default null (all SKUs).
skus.title: Skus

page_index.description: Optional. Page number (integer), starts from 1. Default 1.
page_index.title: Page Index

page_size.description: Optional. Rows per page (integer). Min 5, max 1000. Default 50.
page_size.title: Page Size

sort_by.description: Optional. Metric to sort product rows by. Rows are ordered by the metric's value over the queried date range. If omitted, server default order applies. Allowed values: sales, units_sold, units_returned, refund, promo, advertising_cost, amazon_fees, reimbursements, estimated_payout, cost_of_goods, gross_revenue, gross_profit, expenses, indirect_cost, net_profit, margin, roi, tacos, ads_acos, refunds_percentage, sessions. Cost-type metrics (refund, promo, advertising_cost, amazon_fees, cost_of_goods, expenses, indirect_cost) are returned as negative values and are ordered by ABSOLUTE amount, not signed value: sort_order=desc lists the highest spend/cost first and asc the lowest.
sort_by.title: Sort By

sort_order.description: Optional. Sort direction for sort_by. 'desc' = highest value first (default); 'asc' = lowest value first. Ignored if sort_by is not provided.
sort_order.title: Sort Order

CostConfigCaveat.description:
A zero cost metric that may mean "never configured" (spec HP-1483 §6 / HP-2033).

``cost_of_goods`` / ``indirect_cost`` come back as 0 both when the real cost is
zero and when the seller never configured one — the P&L response cannot tell
those apart, and the difference decides whether the profit figures mean
anything. QA found an agent reading ``indirect_cost: 0`` as "data completely
normal" on an account whose net_profit was inflated by two unconfigured cost
lines, so the ambiguity is stated in the payload rather than left to be inferred.

Deliberately NOT a ``configured: false`` assertion: this response has no way to
know that (see :func:`_flag_unconfigured_costs`), and asserting it would repeat
the very error the caveat exists to prevent.

metric.description: The zero metric this caveat is about, e.g. 'indirect_cost'.
metric.title: Metric

message.description: What the zero does and does not establish, and what it distorts.
message.title: Message

affects.description: Metric keys present in this response whose values are distorted while the zero is unexplained. Do not report them as reliable until verified.
affects.title: Affects

verify_with.description: Tools that settle whether the cost is configured. Call before concluding.
verify_with.title: Verify With

CostConfigCaveat.title: CostConfigCaveat

total_count.title: Total Count

caveats.description: Zero-cost ambiguities detected in this response (HP-2033). Absent when there is nothing to flag. A cost metric of 0 does not establish that the cost is really zero — it is equally consistent with the seller never having configured it — so each entry names the distorted metrics and the tools that settle it. Resolve these before characterising the profit figures.
caveats.title: Caveats

meta.description: What the returned amounts cover: currency/unit, the resolved timezone and marketplaces, and the window actually queried. Check period_days against the other period before quoting any percentage change (HP-2032).

asin.description: Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) of the child product variant, e.g. '[REDACTED:PUBLIC_EXAMPLE_IDENTIFIER]'. Null when the product level is parent_asin.
asin.title: Asin

parent_asin.description: Parent ASIN that groups child variants (e.g. different sizes/colours). Populated at all product levels; null when not applicable.
parent_asin.title: Parent Asin

sku.description: Seller-defined SKU, unique within a seller account. Reliably populated when product_level=sku. At asin/parent_asin level: typically null in non-series tools, but may be non-null in *_series tools; use asin/parent_asin for identity matching.
sku.title: Sku

product_name.description: Amazon product listing title as it appears on the detail page. May be null if the product metadata is not available.
product_name.title: Product Name

brand.description: Brand name associated with the product as registered in Amazon Brand Registry or the seller's catalog. Null when not available.
brand.title: Brand

image_url.description: HTTPS URL of the main product image thumbnail served by Amazon. Null when the product has no image or metadata is unavailable.
image_url.title: Image Url

marketplace.description: Amazon marketplace short country code where this product is sold (e.g. 'US', 'CA', 'UK'). Same vocabulary as the 'marketplace' filter parameter — this value can be fed straight back as a filter.
marketplace.title: Marketplace

seller_id.description: Amazon seller account ID (merchant token) that owns this product listing, e.g. '[REDACTED:PUBLIC_EXAMPLE_IDENTIFIER]'. Corresponds to the seller_ids filter parameter.
seller_id.title: Seller Id

metrics.description: Per-product flat metric map for the requested date range. Flat map of metric_key → numeric value. Monetary amounts (float, rounded to 2 decimal places, denominated in the requested currency). Expenditure metrics (refund, promo, advertising_cost, amazon_fees, cost_of_goods, expenses, indirect_cost) are returned as NEGATIVE values (cash outflows). Income metrics (sales, reimbursements, estimated_payout, gross_revenue, gross_profit, net_profit) are positive when the period is profitable. Per-metric notes: sales — gross sales revenue before any deductions; refund — total refund/return amount (negative, expenditure); promo — promotional discounts (negative, expenditure); advertising_cost — total ad spend across Sponsored Products, Brands, Display (negative, expenditure); amazon_fees — all Amazon platform fees: FBA, referral, etc. (negative, expenditure); reimbursements — Amazon reimbursement credits; estimated_payout — estimated settlement payout from Amazon; cost_of_goods — seller-defined cost of goods sold / COGS (negative, expenditure); gross_revenue — top-line revenue (sales minus refunds); gross_profit — gross_revenue minus amazon_fees and cost_of_goods; expenses — total operating expenses (negative, expenditure); indirect_cost — overhead / indirect costs allocated to this period (negative, expenditure); net_profit — bottom-line profit after all deductions. Rate/percentage values (float, rounded to 2 decimal places, expressed as a percentage, e.g. 21.01 means 21.01%): margin — net profit margin (net_profit / gross_revenue × 100); roi — return on investment (net_profit / cost_of_goods × 100); tacos — TACoS (attr 1 day): ad spend / total sales, using Profits 1-day attribution for ad spend alignment; measures ad spend impact on total sales and profitability (advertising_cost / gross_revenue × 100); ads_acos — ACoS (attr 1 day): ACOS based on Profits ad sales (1-day attribution, SKU-level SP/SD only); use mainly for profit, same-day, or organic sales analysis — for general advertising performance prefer Ads ACOS (advertising_cost / ad-attributed sales × 100); refunds_percentage — refund rate (refund / gross_revenue × 100). Count metrics (integer, e.g. 6): units_sold — total units ordered; units_returned — total units returned/refunded; sessions — unique visitor sessions on product detail pages. A key is omitted when its value is null for the period.
metrics.title: Metrics

ResponseMeta.description:
What the returned amounts cover (HP-1674/1677, HP-2032).

Present on every P&L response. Declared here because it has been on the wire
since HP-1674 without appearing in any outputSchema — which made ``period_days``
useless as the cross-period check HP-2032 needs it to be.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency every amount is expressed in. Amounts originate in each marketplace's local currency and are CONVERTED into this one per marketplace before being aggregated — figures spanning several marketplaces are therefore comparable, not a raw sum of mixed currencies. One exchange rate is applied across the whole requested range rather than each day's historical rate, so a period-over-period change can carry some FX movement that is not a change in the underlying business.
currency.title: Currency

fx_converted.description: Always true for these tools. Every amount has already been converted into `currency`; none is a raw local-marketplace figure, and a multi-marketplace total is NOT a mixed-currency sum. Do not state or imply otherwise — a response carrying this flag has been checked against the backend, and claiming the figures are unconverted contradicts the payload.
fx_converted.title: Fx Converted

unit.description: Always 'major' — amounts are not in cents.
unit.title: Unit

display_ready.description: True: amounts can be shown as-is, no /100.
display_ready.title: Display Ready

date_tz.description: IANA timezone the day boundaries were resolved in.
date_tz.title: Date Tz

marketplaces.description: Marketplace short codes the amounts cover, or 'all_authorised' when the request did not narrow it. 'all_authorised' means the figures are the combined total across EVERY marketplace this account is authorised for, not one storefront — say so when reporting them, since the caller did not choose that. Converted into a single currency first (see currency).
marketplaces.title: Marketplaces

period_from.description: First day actually queried (YYYY-MM-DD), after validation and the future-end-day clamp. May differ from what was requested.
period_from.title: Period From

period_to.description: Last day actually queried (YYYY-MM-DD), after validation and the future-end-day clamp. May differ from what was requested.
period_to.title: Period To

period_days.description: Inclusive length of the queried window in days. When comparing two periods, read this from BOTH responses and require them to be equal before quoting any percentage change: comparing a 30-day window with a 31-day one inflates every delta (~2pp on a monthly comparison). If they differ, align the windows, switch to daily averages, or state the difference and its effect on every percentage reported.
period_days.title: Period Days

ResponseMeta.title: ResponseMeta

notice.description: Optional non-blocking advisory (spec §6.1). Present only when the platform attaches one — currently a quota near-limit reminder (code QUOTA_NEAR_LIMIT). Null/absent on the vast majority of responses. Independent of 'error': the call still succeeded.

data.description: Paginated product-level P&L summary for the requested date range. Null when no matching data exists (e.g. seller_ids filter yields no authorised sellers).

error.description: Null on success; error object on failure.

generate_if_missing.description: When true (default), run OpenAI Whisper on the ad video if no stored transcript exists. Paid plans only.

original.description: Fetch or generate the Whisper video transcript for one Meta ad (full script plus timestamped segments). Uses the same ad_url_or_id formats as scan_ad — prefer context.ad.id or context.public_share_url from WinningHunter ad detail JSON. Returns a cached transcript from MongoDB when available; otherwise runs OpenAI Whisper on the ad video when generate_if_missing is true (default). Generating new transcripts requires a paid plan.
